Mechanism: clash_report (services/leases/common.py) enriches each clash clause with held_for text from lease.acquired_at and a lease->epoch activity reader. Refute: a refus-a-agent sees a clause with no 'held for'/'last write'. Test tests/test_lease_release_early.py asserts both phrases and fails against the unfixed code (the kwargs now=/activity= and the note are new).

Governing rules and decisions read and applied: D-lock-lifecycle-answers (release at merge-ready, re-acquire per file), D-lease-lifecycle-automation-2026-11-11 (leases follow the work), D-lease-hold-limit (idleness measured by work not heartbeat, r-lock-cycle-selfheal, r-everything-configurable, r-reuse-core, r-small-files). evidence.note: Claim: a merge can record every rename/move/package split as a self-contained path.moved event derived from git diff --name-status -M plus the X -> X/__init__.py split shape, replayable from the log alone. Mechanism: drift.moves_between; refuted if a merge that renames a file records no path.moved. Probe (python temp repo): a.py moved to src/b.py -> Move(old=a.py,new=src/b.py,how=rename). Test tests/test_path_moves.py asserts detection + a real merge records path.moved into state.moves.

Governing rules applied: r-reuse-core (extends services.drift, the single drift function, no second drift), r-small-files, r-everything-configurable (ages/moves are facts not policy; no new knob needed), D-universal-principles, DX-drift-core (single source for MV-* and freshness), the detector reuses CH.changed_paths/git -M, no model call. Event kind path.moved declared with its upgrade-manifest entry in the same change (coherence clean: declared AND fold-handled).

Implemented: drift.Move + moves_between (rename via git -M; split = D X + A X/__init__.py); _record_moves in api/lifecycle/merge.py records one path.moved per move; State.moves field + _h_path_moved fold handler; templates/events/moves.toml + event_kind_added.path.moved.toml manifest; tests/test_path_moves.py. Verified detection on a throwaway repo (a.py->src/b.py rename detected) and event-kind coherence (declared+handled, 0 problems).

chunk_findings.detail: `_record_moves` is invoked as `_record_moves(log, repo, item, landed_before, branch_head, sha)`, using the branch tip as the “after” commit rather than the landed commit. The nearby `_record_reconciled` call receives both `landed_after` and `branch_head`, so those values are not guaranteed to be the same. For a non-fast-forward merge where the branch tip contains a rename/delete/add pair that the merge result does not actually land (for example, the branch renames `a.py` to `b.py`, but the merge retains `a.py` or resolves the conflict differently), `git` diffing `landed_before..branch_head` will report a move and `_record_moves` will append a `path.moved` event for a move that did not land. Conversely, moves that appear only in the merge result but not in `branch_head` are missed. The stated detector is supposed to record moves from the merge/landing diff, so this can produce wrong replayable move history.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/merge.py:_record_moves call site

chunk_findings.detail: When `DR.moves_between` returns `None` to signal that git could not answer, `_record_moves` simply returns and records no event. Because `State.moves` defaults to an empty list and no unavailable marker is recorded, replaying the merge yields the same state as a merge that genuinely had no moves. This makes “git unavailable” indistinguishable from “no moves” in the folded state, contrary to the change’s own invariant that an unavailable check must not be treated as a passed/no-move result.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/merge.py:_record_moves

chunk_findings.detail: `moves_between` treats any deleted path as a package-split candidate after stripping only the final extension. Given a commit that deletes `foo.py` and `foo.txt` and adds `foo/__init__.py`, git diff yields `D foo.py`, `D foo.txt`, `A foo/__init__.py`; `foo.txt`.rsplit(".", 1)[0] is `foo`, so the function emits a bogus `Move("foo.txt", "foo/__init__.py", "split")`. That non-module file did not move into the package, so the single move source records a false move and corrupts downstream MV-* tasks.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/drift.py:309-311

chunk_findings.detail: The split record is only produced when `__init__.py` appears as an added file, but git rename detection consumes the delete/add pair when enough content survives. Given before `module.py` and after `module/__init__.py` containing the same body plus `module/sub.py`, `git diff --name-status -M` reports `R100 module.py module/__init__.py` and `A module/sub.py`; `deleted` is empty and `added` lacks `__init__.py`. The function returns only a `rename` move, so the package split is misclassified and the fact that the old module became a package is lost, contrary to the docstring and stated intent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/drift.py:302-311

chunk_findings.detail: When git succeeds but cannot classify a many-into-one merge as a rename, the function returns an empty list, which callers will treat as “no moves” rather than unavailable. Given before `a.py` and `b.py` and after `c.py` containing parts of both but below git’s rename threshold, git diff outputs `D a.py`, `D b.py`, `A c.py`; the function finds no `R` and no `__init__.py`, so it returns `[]`. The merge of files is silently dropped, despite the intent claiming many-old/one-new merges are handled and the docstring saying git could not say should not be reported as “nothing moved”.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/drift.py:292-312

chunk_findings.detail: `_claimed` writes `(repo / glob).write_text("x\n")` without creating parent directories. The merge test calls it with `glob="src/a.py"`. The other tests show the `repo` fixture does not pre-create `src` (they call `(repo / "src").mkdir()`), so this line raises `FileNotFoundError` before any claim/merge, making `test_merge_records_a_path_moved_event` fail.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_path_moves.py:_claimed

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims to exercise the package-split shape `X` deleted, `X/__init__.py` added, but deletes `mod.py` and adds `modpkg/__init__.py`. There is no deleted path whose package directory is `modpkg/__init__.py`; for the intended detector (`mod.py` -> `mod/__init__.py`) the range has no matching split, so `moves_between` returns no move and the assertion fails. If a looser detector passes, the test does not verify the required module-to-package split.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_path_moves.py:test_moves_between_detects_a_package_split

chunk_findings.detail: The new call passes `branch_head` as the “after” commit while the event records `sha` (the merge commit). For a non-fast-forward merge, `branch_head` is the branch tip, not necessarily the landed merge result; `_record_reconciled` is given both `landed_after` and `branch_head`, showing those can differ. If the branch renames `a.py` to `b.py`, but the merge resolution keeps `a.py` (for example, main modified `a.py` and the conflict is resolved by taking main’s version and discarding the branch’s `b.py`), `git diff landed_before branch_head` still reports the rename, so `_record_moves` appends `path.moved` with `new="b.py"` and `sha=<merge>`, even though the tree at `sha` never landed that move. Replay then puts a false move into `State.moves`, corrupting the MV-* consumers and freshness drift.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/merge.py:_record_moves call site

chunk_findings.detail: When `DR.moves_between` returns `None` to signal that git could not answer, `_record_moves` returns without recording any event or unavailable marker. Because `State.moves` defaults to an empty list and `_h_path_moved` only appends records when a `path.moved` event exists, a merge whose move detection was unavailable folds to exactly the same state as a merge that genuinely had zero moves. That violates the change’s invariant that an unavailable check must not be treated as passed/no-move; later consumers cannot distinguish “git unavailable” from “no moves” and will silently miss path moves.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/merge.py:_record_moves

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding 4 still holds. A package split is only recorded as `split` when git reports the old module as `D` and `__init__.py` as `A`, but git rename detection normally consumes the `module.py` → `module/__init__.py` pair when the body survives. Given before `module.py` and after `module/__init__.py` with the same body plus a new `module/sub.py`, `git diff --name-status -M` reports `R100 module.py module/__init__.py` and `A module/sub.py`; `deleted` is empty, so the function returns only `Move("module.py", "module/__init__.py", "rename")`. chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding 5 still holds. A many-into-one merge that git does not classify as a rename returns `[]`, which callers will treat as “no moves” rather than unavailable. Given before `a.py` and `b.py` and after `c.py` containing parts of both below git’s rename threshold, the diff is `D a.py`, `D b.py`, `A c.py`; the function finds no `R` line and no `__init__.py`, so it returns `[]`. chunk_findings.detail: The merge test calls `_claimed(repo, "T1", "src/a.py", "agent-a")`, and `_claimed` does `(repo / glob).write_text("x\n")` without creating the parent directory `repo/src`. The repo fixture does not create `src` (the rename test in the same file has to call `(repo / "src").mkdir()`), so this write raises `FileNotFoundError` before any claim or merge can run. This is the same previously reported defect; the current diff does not add the missing parent-directory creation.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_path_moves.py:45 (`_claimed`)

chunk_findings.detail: The test says it covers the intended package-split shape `X` deleted, `X/__init__.py` added, but it deletes `mod.py` and adds `modpkg/__init__.py`. `modpkg` is not the package directory produced by splitting `mod.py` (that would be `mod/__init__.py`), so with the intended detector this range should not produce a move matching `old="mod.py"` and `new` containing `modpkg/__init__.py`, and the assertion fails. If the detector does pass this test, it is pairing an unrelated deleted module with an unrelated added `__init__.py`, which contradicts the stated package-split rule. This is the same previously reported test-shape defect; the current diff still uses `modpkg` rather than `mod`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_path_moves.py:70 (`test_moves_between_detects_a_package_split`)

chunk_findings.detail: Given a merge where `DR.moves_between` returns `None` (git detection unavailable), `_record_moves` emits a `path.moved` event with `old=""`, `new=""`, and `how="unavailable"`. `_h_path_moved` only checks that the four keys exist and appends that dict to `State.moves`, which is documented as “One record per move” and is the single move source. Thus after a git failure `State.moves` contains a non-move sentinel with empty paths, so `bool(state.moves)` is true and any consumer that iterates `state.moves` as moves sees a bogus move from `""` to `""`. The unavailable condition should be kept separate from the move list, or the handler must not append it to `State.moves`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/model.py:_h_path_moved

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding 2 still holds. The split classification only runs over paths collected from `D` lines, so when git’s `-M` detects the package split as a rename from `module.py` to `module/__init__.py`, `deleted` is empty and the move is recorded as `rename`, not `split`. chunk_findings.detail: `moves_between` parses `git diff --name-status` output by splitting each line on tab and using the raw fields as file paths, but Git quotes paths containing characters such as `"` or `\` even when `core.quotepath=off` is passed. For example, if a merge renames a file literally named `foo"bar.py` to `foo"baz.py`, Git can emit `R100\t"foo\"bar.py"\t"foo\"baz.py"`; the function then returns `Move(old='\"foo\\\"bar.py\"', new='\"foo\\\"baz.py\"', ...)` (with the Git quoting/escaping included) instead of the actual tracked paths. Downstream path-move records and freshness tracking then reference paths that do not exist in the tree.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/drift.py `moves_between` parsing loop

chunk_findings.detail: The integration test only checks that some recorded move has `new == "src/b.py"`. If `_h_path_moved` or the event payload were wrong and recorded only `{"new": "src/b.py"}` (or recorded the wrong `old`/`sha`) the assertion still passes, so the test does not enforce the change's stated contract that each move record contains the old path, new path, and merge sha. For example, a regression where the merge records `{"new": "src/b.py", "how": "rename"}` without `old` or `sha` would satisfy this test while violating the intent.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `-z` parser assumes that only rename (`R`) records carry two path fields and that every other status carries one. Git’s `--name-status` format also has copy records (`C`) with two paths, and copy detection can be enabled by repository configuration (`diff.renames=copies`) even though the command passes only `-M`. If a copy record is emitted, e.g. the `-z` stream is `C100\0old.py\0new.py\0A\0added.py\0`, the parser sets `n=1` for `C100`, consumes only `old.py`, then treats `new.py` as the next status and consumes `A` as its path. The real added path `added.py` is then treated as a status token and skipped, so the added set is wrong and subsequent records are shifted. If the copy’s new path begins with `R`, the loop can even record a bogus `Move(old='A', new='added.py', how='rename')`. Thus the detector can return wrong move records rather than a correct empty/unavailable result. [D-universal-principles]

data.probe: Fixed: moves_between forces -c diff.renames=true (rename-only, no copies) and defensively parses a C record as 2 fields (adds its destination, never records a move for a copy -- a copy is not a move).
